rejected.file: File:St Casimir Church Cleveland, Ohio. Interior.jpg and File:Detail High Altar St. Casimir Church Cleveland, Ohio.jpg (both by Owen M. Dabek)
rejected.reason: Both images depict the HISTORIC POLISH St. Casimir Church at 8223 Sowinski Ave, Cleveland -- not our record's Lithuanian-heritage St. Casimir parish. Evidence: (1) both are captioned "...following Mass Mob" dated March 13, 2016; the documented "Cleveland Mass Mob XX Saint Casimir" event was held 11:30am Sunday March 13, 2016 specifically at 8223 Sowinski Avenue (the Polish national parish, 2nd-oldest Polish parish in Cleveland, founded 1891/92, monumental church completed 1918, closed 2009 and reopened by the Vatican in 2012 as a personal parish for Catholics of Polish descent). (2) The Commons category for these files is "Saint Casimir Church (Cleveland)", which is the English Wikipedia article specifically about that Polish parish building, and the images are used on Wikipedia in articles about "Polish Cathedral style" architecture. Our record's St. Casimir (parishes.json slug sv-kazimiero-cleveland-oh) is a distinct parish: formed Oct 25 2009 from the merger of the Lithuanian Sv. Jurgio (St. George) and DMNP (Our Lady of Perpetual Help) parishes, and it occupies the former Our Lady of Perpetual Help building on Neff Road in Cleveland's Collinwood neighborhood -- a different building at a different address entirely, coincidentally renamed after the same saint. No Wikimedia Commons photos of the Neff Road building were found in this pass.

rejected.file: Carol M. Highsmith photo, LOC LCCN 2012631258 / LC-DIG-highsm-19850, catalogued as "Holy Trinity Church, Hartford, Connecticut"
rejected.reason: The LOC catalog title matches, but the photograph itself is of a completely different, unrelated building: visually the image shows a single-tower Gothic Revival red sandstone church, and a zoomed inspection of the entrance signage reads "TRINITY [Episcopal Church shield] CHURCH -- Sunday Services 8:00 a.m. & 10:00 a.m." This is Trinity Episcopal Church at 120 Sigourney Street, Hartford -- a different denomination, building, and address from Holy Trinity Roman Catholic (Lithuanian) Church at 53 Capitol Avenue (confirmed against the correct building in the Litnet 2000 Commons photo, which shows a twin-towered brick facade with the Latin inscription ECCLESIA SANCTISSIMA TRINITATIS -- architecturally nothing like the Highsmith photo). This appears to be a Library of Congress / Highsmith cataloging mismatch. Rejected as not our parish's building; the two Commons file candidates for this slug are cleared instead (see verified list).
